question: If A = (2)/(3)+(4)/(7) of (14)/(12) and B = (5)/(12) of (7)/(15)times(36)/(21), then what is the value of A + B?
solution:
**Given:**

A = (2)/(3)+(4)/(7) of (14)/(12) and B = (5)/(12) of (7)/(15)times(36)/(21)

Concept used:

Follow the BODMAS rule according to the table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47485e25d1b30c57dc271863db8b99be0c8e209069b2596cc885911d898a8a78.png] 

**Calculation:**

A = (2)/(3)+(4)/(7) of (14)/(12)

⇒ A = (2)/(3)+(2)/(3)

⇒ A = (4)/(3)

⇒ B= (5)/(12)of(7)/(15)times(36)/(21)

⇒ B = (1)/(3)times(3)/(3)

⇒ B = (1)/(3)

Now A + B,

⇒ A + B = 4/3 + 1/3

⇒ A + B = 5/3

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**
